04/ 15.07.2024  I.A. No.4196 of 2024 This Interlocutory Application has been filed by the appellant praying therein to suspend the sentence and release him on bail during pendency of this appeal.
2. The appellant has been convicted and sentenced in connection with POCSO Case No.93 of 2018.
He has been convicted for the offences under Sections 376(D)(A), 306/34 IPC and Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act.
He was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 20 years with a fine of Rs.20,000/- under Section 376(D)(A) of the IPC along with other sentences for other offences.
3. No one appears on behalf of the State.
Heard, learned counsel for the appellant and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4. This is a case where a girl of 16 years was gang raped.
The allegation of rape is against this appellant, one Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh & others.
The girl two days thereafter committed suicide by burning herself.

The appellant prays for suspension of sentence and to release him on bail only on the ground that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has granted bail to Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh considering the period of his custody.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh was in custody for five and a half years when the bail was granted and this appellant is Ajay Sahu vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45780797/

sentences.text: He submits that the case of Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh and this appellant cannot be differentiated as the allegation against them are exactly the same.
6. After going through the allegations against this appellant and Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh, we find that the allegations against Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh and this appellant are exactly the same.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court considered the case of Bhairo Yadav @ Bind Singh in Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.13131 of 2023 and released him on bail vide order dated 16th January, 2024 which reads as here under:-
"1. Leave granted.
2. Perused the findings of the Trial Court on the allegations of rape.
The appellant has undergone incarceration for a period of about five and a half years.
The appeal against conviction is not likely to be heard in near future.

3. Therefore, in the facts of the case, the appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail,
pending final disposal of the appeal before the High Court.
4. For that purpose, the appellant shall be produced before the Trial Court within a period of one week from today.
5. The Trial Court shall enlarge the appellant on bail on appropriate terms and conditions.
The learned Public Prosecutor will be heard before fixing terms and conditions of bail.
6. The appeal is, accordingly, allowed on the above terms.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of."

7. Since the case of this appellant stands on exactly similar footing, considering the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.13131 of 2023 releasing Bhairo Yadav @
Bind Singh, we are inclined to release this appellant on bail.

8. Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellant is directed to be released on bail during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-IV- cum-Special Judge (POCSO) at Ranchi, in POCSO Case No.93 of 2018, with a condition that the appellant shall appear and mark his attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court,
Ranchi, once in every four months till the disposal of this Appeal.
9. This interlocutory application is, accordingly, allowed.
(ANANDA SEN, J.) (GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.)
